title: Demand Service Rate Programs: How Large a Prepaid Block the Drawing Record Calls For
content:
Where the shortfall stands above one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples, as many whole multiples
are sold as it takes to cover the shortfall, rounded up. Where there is no shortfall at all, no multiple
is sold. In any other case neither term above changes the number of multiples sold.

The prepaid hours standing are the hours of every block bought within the tier's expiry period less the
hours drawn over the window read, never below nil, and the shortfall is the hours drawn over that window
less the prepaid hours standing, never below nil.

The minimum purchase each program publishes under the Demand Service Rate Programs:

| Program | Minimum purchase (hours) |
|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 0 |
| Priority Response Program | 0 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 40 |
| Emergency Response Program | 40 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 60 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 100 |

| The shortfall against the tier's minimum purchase | The multiples sold |
|---|---|
| above one minimum purchase | as many whole multiples as it takes to cover it, rounded up |
| above nil, at or below one minimum purchase | neither term above changes the number sold |
| none at all | none |

**Both sides of the figure (hypothetical).** On the Critical Facility Response Program, whose minimum
purchase is 60 hours: a shortfall of 61 hours stands above one minimum purchase, so 2 whole multiples
are sold, 2 being what it takes to cover 61 hours when rounded up. A shortfall of 60 hours stands at one
minimum purchase rather than above it. A shortfall of 130 hours calls for 3 whole multiples. Where the
prepaid hours standing are at least the hours drawn, there is no shortfall and no multiple is sold.
